label: Bloc member house
summary: Bloc member houses: all houses that have joined a house bloc, the leading house among them.
details: `[bloc_member_houses|E]` shows the words Bloc Member Houses, linked to the Bloc Member House concept; vanilla uses it in the house bloc and cohesion explanations.

label: Bloc member ruler
summary: A bloc member ruler: a ruler who belongs to a house bloc.
details: `[bloc_member_ruler|E]` shows the words Bloc Member Ruler, linked to the explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Bloc member ruler
summary: Bloc member rulers: the rulers who belong to a house bloc.
details: `[bloc_member_rulers|E]` shows the words Bloc Member Rulers, linked to the Bloc Member Ruler concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: House bloc
summary: The possessive form of bloc, a defensive alliance of houses within a realm.
details: `[bloc_possessive|E]` shows the word Bloc's, linked to the House Bloc concept. Vanilla uses it once, in a text about a bloc's aspiration.

label: Bloc member ruler
summary: A bloc member ruler: any ruler who is a member of a house bloc.
details: `[bloc_ruler|E]` shows the words Bloc Ruler, linked to the Bloc Member Ruler concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Bloc member ruler
summary: Bloc member rulers: the rulers who are members of a house bloc.
details: `[bloc_rulers|E]` shows the words Bloc Rulers, linked to the Bloc Member Ruler concept. Vanilla uses it in the confederation window's counts of individual and total bloc rulers.

label: Bloc supremacy war
summary: A bloc supremacy war: a special war between the leading houses of two soryo house blocs, which every member of both blocs joins.
details: The winning bloc gains cohesion and the losing bloc loses a third of its cohesion; some soryo member houses of the losing bloc, depending on their house head's ties to the losing leader, switch to the winning bloc. `[bloc_supremacy|E]` shows the words Bloc Supremacy, linked to the Bloc Supremacy War concept; vanilla uses it in advice texts.

label: Bloc supremacy war
summary: A bloc supremacy war: an all-out war between the leading houses of two soryo house blocs, joined by all members of both.
details: The winning bloc gains cohesion, the losing one loses a third of its cohesion. `[bloc_supremacy_war|E]` shows the words Bloc Supremacy War, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the war's name.

label: House bloc
summary: House blocs: defensive alliances of houses within a realm, whose members defend any attacked member house.
details: `[blocs|E]` shows the word Blocs, linked to the House Bloc concept. Vanilla uses it in government texts ("Uses blocs") and in a rule about the heads of leading houses.

label: Blood brother
summary: A blood brother: a special kind of friend and ally who becomes a symbolic member of the family.
details: A character can have only one, and it must be someone who is not already family. Refusing a blood brother's call to war breaks the bond and makes them rivals. Blood brothers, their children and their primary spouses like each other more. `[blood_brother|E]` shows the words Blood Brother, linked to the explanation.

label: Blood brother
summary: The possessive form of blood brother, a friend and ally who becomes a symbolic family member.
details: Its text in the game is "Best Friend's", not "Blood Brother's", so `[blood_brother_possessive|E]` shows Best Friend's while linking to the Blood Brother concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Blood brother
summary: Blood brotherhood: the bond of a blood brother, a friend and ally who counts as symbolic family.
details: `[blood_brotherhood|E]` shows the words Blood Brotherhood, linked to the Blood Brother concept. Vanilla uses it in an interaction text about a blood brotherhood linking two characters.

label: Blood brother
summary: Blood brothers: two characters bound as special friends and allies, each a symbolic member of the other's family.
details: `[blood_brothers|E]` shows the words Blood Brothers, linked to the Blood Brother concept. Vanilla uses it in opinion and achievement texts.

label: Blood brother
summary: The plural possessive of blood brother, a friend and ally who becomes symbolic family.
details: Its text in the game is "Best Friends'", so `[blood_brothers_possessive|E]` shows Best Friends' while linking to the Blood Brother concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Match
summary: A board game: two players pitting luck and skill against each other, as a friendly match or for a wager.
details: There are several board game types; winning and playing work the same in all of them, only the skills used differ. `[board_game|E]` shows the words Board Game, linked to the Match concept. Vanilla uses it in the description of the interaction to play a board game.

label: Match
summary: A board game match between two players, played for fun or for a wager.
details: `[board_game_game|E]` shows the word Game, linked to the Match concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Match
summary: A board game match: a contest of wits and chance between two players, friendly or with a wager.
details: `[board_game_match|E]` shows the word Match, linked to the explanation. Vanilla uses it in the results of board game events ("I win the match against ...").

label: Board game type
summary: The kind of board game being played, which decides which play styles counter which.
details: In a board game, play styles counter each other: countering an opponent's move greatly cuts the points they gain from it, even when it succeeds, and skilled opponents may try to counter you. The games are chess, pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go and fidchell. `[board_game_type|E]` shows the words Board Game Type, linked to the explanation; no vanilla text uses this name.

label: Chess
summary: Chess, a board game type in which martial counters learning, learning counters intrigue, and intrigue counters martial.
details: Countering an opponent's play style greatly cuts the points they gain from a move. `[board_game_type_chess|E]` shows the word Chess, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Board game type
summary: The word "counter" of board games: one play style countering another, which greatly cuts the points the countered player gains.
details: Its text is the lowercase word counter, which the game's board game type explanations use inside their sentences. `[board_game_type_counter|E]` shows it, linked to the Board Game Type concept. No vanilla text uses it in brackets.

label: Board game type
summary: The word "counters" of board games, as in "martial counters learning": one play style beating another.
details: Each board game type's explanation lists which skill counters which with this word. `[board_game_type_counters|E]` shows it, linked to the Board Game Type concept. No vanilla text uses it in brackets.

label: Fidchell
summary: Fidchell, a board game type in which learning counters prowess, prowess counters diplomacy, and diplomacy counters learning.
details: `[board_game_type_fidchell|E]` shows the word Fidchell, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Go
summary: Go, a board game type in which learning counters martial, martial counters intrigue, and intrigue counters learning.
details: `[board_game_type_go|E]` shows the word Go, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Hnefatafl
summary: Hnefatafl, a board game type in which intrigue counters martial, martial counters prowess, and prowess counters intrigue.
details: `[board_game_type_hnefatafl|E]` shows the word Hnefatafl, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Pachisi
summary: Pachisi, a board game type in which diplomacy counters intrigue, intrigue counters stewardship, and stewardship counters diplomacy.
details: `[board_game_type_pachisi|E]` shows the word Pachisi, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Tabula
summary: Tabula, a board game type in which intrigue counters learning, learning counters stewardship, and stewardship counters intrigue.
details: `[board_game_type_tabula|E]` shows the word Tabula, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the board game events.

label: Board game type
summary: Board game types: the kinds of board game, each with its own set of play styles that counter each other.
details: `[board_game_types|E]` shows the words Board Game Types, linked to the Board Game Type concept. Vanilla uses it in the board game match explanation.

label: Winning
summary: Winning a board game: by getting far ahead of the opponent in score, or by being the defending player when there is no clear winner after the last round.
details: The last round is set by the script value `bg_round_cap_value`. `[board_game_win|E]` shows the word Win, linked to the Winning concept; vanilla uses it in the board game match explanation.

label: Winning
summary: How a board game is won: a large lead in score, or being the defender when no one has clearly won after the last round.
details: `[board_game_winning|E]` shows the word Winning, linked to the explanation. Vanilla uses it in board game event options that give score towards winning.

label: Winning
summary: Winning a board game, which happens by a large score lead or by defending until the round limit with no clear winner.
details: `[board_game_winning_sudden_death|E]` shows the words Sudden Death, linked to the Winning concept. Vanilla uses it in the results of board game events.

label: Match
summary: Board games: contests of wits and chance between two players, friendly or with a wager.
details: `[board_games|E]` shows the words Board Games, linked to the Match concept. Vanilla uses it in accolade and cultural tradition texts.

label: Border raid
summary: A border raid: a special war between rulers involved in the Iberian struggle, in which the attacker besieges one enemy county on their border.
details: The war leader gains gold for taking the target county, which loses development and control. Buildings may be destroyed for more gold, more likely with high development and a large besieging army. `[border_raid|E]` shows the words Border Raid, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the war's name and in a rule that fealty cannot be bargained over one.

label: Border raid
summary: Border raiding: the special Iberian struggle war of besieging one enemy county on your border for gold.
details: `[border_raiding|E]` shows the words Border Raiding, linked to the Border Raid concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Border raid
summary: Border raids: special wars of the Iberian struggle in which the attacker besieges a bordering enemy county.
details: `[border_raids|E]` shows the words Border Raids, linked to the Border Raid concept. Vanilla uses it in a struggle catalyst about starting border raids on a neighbouring county.

label: Breeding
summary: Breeding: arranging marriages between characters with good congenital traits so that their children inherit them.
details: Lucky children may even get a stronger version of a trait, but bad congenital traits are passed on the same way. Marrying close relatives for better traits risks inbreeding. `[bred|E]` shows the word Bred, linked to the Breeding concept; vanilla uses it in the spouse and trait explanations.

label: Breeding
summary: Breeding: matching characters with good inherited (congenital) traits in marriage so their children get them too.
details: `[breed|E]` shows the word Breed, linked to the Breeding concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Breeding
summary: Breeding: arranging marriages to pass good congenital traits on to children, which can also pass on bad ones.
details: Marrying close relatives to get better traits carries the risk of inbreeding. `[breeding|E]` shows the word Breeding, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the congenital trait explanation.

label: Build pilgrim roads
summary: A decision to build roads that make life easier for pilgrims.
details: The concept's name is the decision's own name, Build Pilgrim Roads. `[build_holy_pilgrim_roads_decision|E]` shows it, linked to the explanation. Vanilla uses it in a struggle parameter that unlocks the decision.

label: Builder
summary: The icon of the Builder personality: a ruler who wants to put all their gold into the realm.
details: Builders empty their treasury for buildings and men-at-arms, often add economic buildings and holdings, and save only when directly threatened, for example by a strong faction; they are slightly less likely to create and promote legends. `builder_i` is another name of this concept whose text is just its icon (`@builder_icon!`). Vanilla writes `[builder_i]` before the personality's name and in a law text about subjects leaning to this personality.

label: Building
summary: A building: an improvement that can be built in a holding.
details: Many buildings can only go in certain baronies or terrain. Each holding has a limited number of building slots, and county capitals get one extra; duchy buildings and special buildings use slots of their own. `[building|E]` shows the word Building, linked to the explanation, and vanilla uses it widely.

label: Building
summary: Buildings: improvements built in holdings, each holding with a limited number of slots.
details: Some can only be built in certain baronies or terrain; county capitals have an extra slot. `[buildings|E]` shows the word Buildings, linked to the Building concept, and vanilla uses it widely.

label: Papal bull
summary: A papal bull: a solemn decree by the head of a Christian faith, backed by the authority of the Christian Church.
details: A Christian head of faith with enough church authority proclaims one through a decision, spending piety, for example to call a great holy war, denounce a rite as heresy, or declare a core tenet permitted. `[bull|E]` shows the word Bull, linked to the Papal Bull concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Bully
summary: Bullies: cruel children who pick on another child, their victim.
details: On coming of age a bully may become a rival, or grow out of it. `[bullies|E]` shows the word Bullies, linked to the Bully concept; vanilla uses it in court position texts and in the trigger text that counts bullies.

label: Bully
summary: The plural possessive of bully, a cruel child who picks on another child.
details: `[bullies_possessive|E]` shows the word Bullies', linked to the Bully concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Papal bull
summary: Papal bulls: solemn decrees of a Christian head of faith, proclaimed through a decision for piety.
details: `[bulls|E]` shows the word Bulls, linked to the Papal Bull concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Bully
summary: A bully: a cruel child who picks on another child, their victim, for fun, gain or boredom.
details: On reaching adulthood, a bully may become a rival or may grow out of the hate. `[bully|E]` shows the word Bully, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the texts of the effects that make someone a bully.

label: Bully
summary: The possessive form of bully, a cruel child who picks on another child.
details: `[bully_possessive|E]` shows the word Bully's, linked to the Bully concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Buy artifact claim
summary: An interaction to buy a personal claim on an artifact, paid for with piety or prestige.
details: The concept's name is the interaction's own name, Buy Artifact Claim. `[buy_artifact_claim|E]` shows it, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the perk text about gaining a claim on another character's artifact.

label: Buy artifact claim
summary: The interaction to buy personal artifact claims in exchange for piety or prestige.
details: `[buy_artifact_claim_interaction|E]` shows the words Buy Artifact Claim Interaction, linked to the Buy Artifact Claim concept. Vanilla uses it in an effect text that unlocks the interaction.

label: Buy claim
summary: An interaction to buy an unpressed claim on a title, paid for with piety.
details: Limits: a vassal cannot buy a claim on their liege's titles nor a liege on their vassal's; kings and emperors cannot buy claims on kingdom titles, and emperors not on other empires; nobody can buy a claim on their head of faith. `[buy_claim|E]` shows the interaction's name, Buy Claim, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in a perk text.

label: Buy claim
summary: The interaction to buy unpressed claims on titles in exchange for piety.
details: `[buy_claim_interaction|E]` shows the words Buy Claim Interaction, linked to the Buy Claim concept. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that unlock the interaction or say you can use it.

label: Cadet branching
summary: A cadet branch: a new house that a member of a house founds so they can be a house head themselves.
details: Every dynasty has a founding house; members of cadet houses can branch off again, so a tree of houses grows within the dynasty. `[cadet_branch|E]` shows the words Cadet Branch, linked to the Cadet Branching concept; vanilla uses it in the texts of the effect that creates one and in an achievement.

label: Cadet branching
summary: Cadet branches: new houses split off from a house by members who want to head their own.
details: `[cadet_branches|E]` shows the words Cadet Branches, linked to the Cadet Branching concept. Vanilla uses it in the dynasty explanation and in a government rule about creating them.

label: Cadet branching
summary: Cadet branching: house members founding their own new house, so a tree of houses grows within a dynasty.
details: `[cadet_branching|E]` shows the words Cadet Branching, linked to the explanation. Vanilla uses it in a struggle catalyst about creating a new house.

label: Camel cavalry
summary: Camel cavalry: mounted men-at-arms that, like light cavalry, are good at scouting and chasing the enemy.
details: They usually counter light cavalry and are countered by spearmen, and they are often strong in desert and dryland terrain. `[camel_cavalry|E]` shows the words Camel Cavalry, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it as the regiment type's name.

label: Camp
summary: A camp: the travelling home of tents, pack animals and people that every landless adventurer has.
details: The camp is the adventurer's domicile and moves across the map with them. Camp buildings give the adventurer strong bonuses in place of counties, and followers such as family and knights travel with them. `[camp|E]` shows the word Camp, linked to the explanation, and vanilla uses it often.

label: Camp upgrade
summary: A camp upgrade: a unique improvement to an adventurer's camp.
details: Technically they are domicile buildings, though many stand for customs or a focus of the camp rather than real structures. Their bonuses include new officers, skill boosts for followers and stronger men-at-arms. `[camp_building|E]` shows the words Camp Upgrade, linked to the explanation.

label: Camp upgrade
summary: Camp upgrades: unique improvements to an adventurer's camp, which give bonuses such as new officers.
details: `[camp_buildings|E]` shows the words Camp Upgrades, linked to the Camp Upgrade concept. Vanilla uses it in camp texts and laws.

label: Camp purpose
summary: A camp purpose: what passes for law in a camp, the shared aim that keeps it together, such as scholarship, sellsword work or restoring a rightful ruler.
details: Different purposes unlock different camp buildings (and with them officers) and lead to different events and event options. `[camp_purpose|E]` shows the words Camp Purpose, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in effect and action texts.

label: Camp purpose
summary: A camp purpose: the shared aim that holds an adventurer's camp together.
details: `[camp_purpose_purpose|E]` shows the word Purpose, linked to the Camp Purpose concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Camp purpose
summary: Camp purposes: the aims that hold adventurers' camps together and act as their law.
details: `[camp_purpose_purposes|E]` shows the word Purposes, linked to the Camp Purpose concept; the concept's own explanation uses this word. No vanilla text uses it in brackets.

label: Camp purpose
summary: Camp purposes: what keeps each adventurer's camp together, and what unlocks its buildings and events.
details: `[camp_purposes|E]` shows the words Camp Purposes, linked to the Camp Purpose concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Camp temperament
summary: Camp temperament: the mood of the important people in a camp, whose grumbling matters a lot there, unlike at a court.
details: A camp with a positive temperament gives the adventurer positive character modifiers; that needs most named characters' opinion to be above a threshold (the define `NDomicile` `TEMPERAMENT_THRESHOLD_HIGH`). `[camp_temperament|E]` shows the words Camp Temperament, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in effect texts about what the temperament scales with.

label: Camp
summary: Camps: the moving homes of landless adventurers, from a small circle of tents to great roving hosts.
details: `[camps|E]` shows the word Camps, linked to the Camp concept. Vanilla uses it in the camp purpose explanation.

label: Candidate score
summary: A candidate score: the score of each character in the line of succession of a theocratic or bureaucratic title, which decides who gets the title at succession.
details: It can be changed in many ways, from schemes to spending influence. `[candidate_score|E]` shows the words Candidate Score, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the texts of effects that change a character's score for a title.

label: Candidate score
summary: Candidate scores: the scores that decide who inherits a theocratic or bureaucratic title.
details: `[candidate_scores|E]` shows the words Candidate Scores, linked to the Candidate Score concept. Vanilla uses it once, in a concept text of the Chinese government.

label: Canonized
summary: Canonization: a dead character being declared a saint, or the faith's equivalent such as a Wali or venerated ancestor, which gives them the Saint trait.
details: It is asked for through a decision, may need the head of faith's blessing, and is sealed by consecrating the saint's burial site, which then draws pious travellers; the remains may give holy relics. `[canonization|E]` shows the word Canonization, linked to the Canonized concept; vanilla uses it in decision texts about improving the chance of it.

label: Canonized
summary: Canonized: a character declared a saint (or the faith's equivalent) after death, gaining the Saint trait.
details: `[canonized|E]` shows the word Canonized, linked to the explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in the faith view.

label: Realm capital
summary: The realm capital: the holding where a ruler and their court live.
details: It has a tax bonus and always goes to the primary heir. Occupying an enemy's capital in a war gives a lot of war score and sometimes lets you imprison members of their family. `[capital|E]` shows the word Capital, linked to the Realm Capital concept, and vanilla uses it often.

label: Capital duchy
summary: The capital duchy modifier: more levies from every holding you hold in the same de jure duchy as your capital, and a bonus for stationed men-at-arms.
details: It only works if you personally hold that duchy, and it does not stack with the realm capital bonus. `[capital_duchy|E]` shows the words Capital Duchy, linked to the explanation. In decision texts, `[capital_duchy.GetBaseNameNoTierNoTooltip]` is something else: a title the decision saved under the name `capital_duchy`.

label: Realm capital
summary: The possessive form of capital, the holding where a ruler and their court live.
details: `[capital_possessive|E]` shows the word Capital's, linked to the Realm Capital concept. Vanilla uses it in texts about the capital's income and its de jure counties.

label: Realm capital
summary: Capitals: the holdings where rulers and their courts live.
details: `[capitals|E]` shows the word Capitals, linked to the Realm Capital concept. Vanilla uses it in event and title view texts.

label: Cardinal
summary: A cardinal: a clergy member chosen by the Pope to further the will of the Christian Church.
details: All members of the College of Cardinals are both candidates and electors for the Papacy, and each has a papabile score. `[cardinal|E]` shows the word Cardinal, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the action to appoint cardinals.

label: Cardinal
summary: The possessive form of cardinal, a clergy member chosen by the Pope.
details: `[cardinal_possessive|E]` shows the word Cardinal's, linked to the Cardinal concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Cardinal
summary: A cardinalate: the position of a cardinal, a clergy member the Pope chose to serve the Christian Church.
details: `[cardinalate|E]` shows the word Cardinalate, linked to the Cardinal concept. Vanilla uses it in an interaction rule that a title must not be a cardinalate; in `[cardinalate.GetName]` the name is instead a title the interaction saved under `cardinalate`.

label: Cardinal
summary: Cardinalates: the positions of cardinals, the clergy chosen by the Pope.
details: `[cardinalates|E]` shows the word Cardinalates, linked to the Cardinal concept. Vanilla uses it once, in an interaction text that a character cannot grant cardinalates.

label: Cardinal
summary: Cardinals: clergy chosen by the Pope, who together elect the next Pope from among themselves.
details: `[cardinals|E]` shows the word Cardinals, linked to the Cardinal concept. Vanilla uses it in the College of Cardinals and succession law texts.

label: Cardinal
summary: The plural possessive of cardinal, a clergy member chosen by the Pope.
details: `[cardinals_possessive|E]` shows the word Cardinals', linked to the Cardinal concept. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Castle holding
summary: A castle: the most heavily fortified holding type, the usual one for feudal, clan and tribal rulers and for holy orders.
details: Castles tend to give more levies than taxes. `[castle|E]` shows the word Castle, linked to the Castle Holding concept; vanilla uses it in decision and holding texts.

label: Castle holding
summary: A castle holding: the most heavily fortified type of holding, which tends to give more levies than taxes.
details: It is the standard holding of feudal, clan and tribal rulers and of holy orders. `[castle_holding|E]` shows the words Castle Holding, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in decision texts.

label: Castle holding
summary: Castle holdings: the most heavily fortified holdings, giving more levies than taxes.
details: `[castle_holdings|E]` shows the words Castle Holdings, linked to the Castle Holding concept. Vanilla uses it in decisions that turn tribal holdings into castles.

label: Castle holding
summary: Castles: the most heavily fortified holding type, standard for feudal, clan and tribal rulers and holy orders.
details: `[castles|E]` shows the word Castles, linked to the Castle Holding concept. Vanilla uses it in the explanation of the holding types.

label: Casualty
summary: Casualties: the soldiers an army loses in a battle, in line with the damage it takes.
details: Soldiers taken out of a battle count either as routed or as dead. `[casualties|E]` shows the word Casualties, linked to the Casualty concept; vanilla uses it in the battle and routed soldier explanations.

label: Casualty
summary: A casualty: a soldier an army loses in battle because of the damage it takes.
details: Lost soldiers are either routed or dead. `[casualty|E]` shows the word Casualty, linked to the explanation; vanilla uses it in the toughness explanation.

label: Casus belli
summary: A casus belli (cause for war): what a ruler needs to declare war on another ruler.
details: It sets what the war is about, usually a certain territory (the war target), and a victory never gains more than it allows. Claims, from succession or the fabricate claim task, are among the most important. `[casus_belli|E]` shows the words Casus Belli, linked to the explanation, and vanilla uses it often.

label: Casus belli
summary: Casus bellis: the causes for war a ruler needs to declare war, each saying what the war can win.
details: `[casus_bellis|E]` shows the words Casus Bellis, linked to the Casus Belli concept. Vanilla uses it in lifestyle and government texts.

label: Ecclesiastical estate
summary: An ecclesiastical estate (also called a cathedral complex): a home tied to a clerical title, standing for the personal lands of an archbishop and their see.
details: Lesser clergy of an ecclesiastical government must rise to such a title before they get one. Its buildings add to the holder's wealth, piety and spiritual fulfillment. The estate does not move and goes to the next holder of the title. `[cathedral_complex|E]` shows the words Cathedral Complex, linked to the Ecclesiastical Estate concept; vanilla uses it in building texts.

label: Ecclesiastical estate building
summary: An ecclesiastical estate building: a unique, lasting improvement to an ecclesiastical estate (cathedral complex).
details: The holder can build many kinds, which give private income, piety and spiritual fulfillment and open up decisions, interactions and more. `[cathedral_complex_building|E]` shows the words Cathedral Complex Building, linked to the Ecclesiastical Estate Building concept. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Ecclesiastical estate building
summary: The game concept Ecclesiastical Estate Building: a lasting improvement built on an ecclesiastical estate, the private landholding of an archbishop's see.
details: `[cathedral_complex_buildings|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation; this key is the plural of the concept's other name, "cathedral complex building". The game's text says the holder builds them for private income, piety, spiritual fulfillment and access to extra decisions and interactions. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Ecclesiastical estate
summary: The game concept Ecclesiastical Estate (also called cathedral complex): a domicile tied to a clerical title, standing for the private lands of an archbishop and their see.
details: `[cathedral_complexes|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation; this key is the plural of the name "cathedral complex". The game's text says the estate stays in one place and passes to the next holder of the title, and buildings can be added to it. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Cautious (icon)
summary: The icon of the game concept Cautious, an AI personality of rulers who prepare to be attacked rather than attack.
details: `[cautious_i|E]` in a text shows the cautious icon linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla puts it in front of the personality's name. Such rulers are somewhat reluctant to start offensive wars, keep gold in reserve, invest in buildings and men-at-arms, and are less likely to create and promote legends.

label: Celestial government
summary: The game concept Celestial Government: a bureaucratic form of government where the liege appoints characters as civilian or military governors.
details: `[celestial|E]` in a text shows the word "Celestial" linked to the concept's explanation. Characters under it use influence, noble families, family mansions and the treasury; independent rulers have legitimacy, while vassals work to gain merit. Vanilla uses the word in texts about the Son of Heaven, government obligations and requirements.

label: Celestial bureaucracy
summary: The game concept Celestial Bureaucracy: how centralized a celestial realm is and how much power its ruler holds over the vassals.
details: `[celestial_bureaucracy|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Only the top liege can change it, celestial vassals share their liege's level, and it has four levels. Vanilla uses it in the government's authority text and in the law texts, including the cooldown after changing it.

label: Celestial government
summary: The game concept Celestial Government: a bureaucratic form of government where the liege appoints characters as civilian or military governors.
details: `[celestial_government|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Characters under it use influence, noble families, family mansions and the treasury; independent rulers have legitimacy, vassals gain merit. Vanilla uses it in the Son of Heaven's concept text.

label: Celestial government (icon)
summary: The icon of the game concept Celestial Government, the bureaucratic government in which the liege appoints governors.
details: `[celestial_i|E]` in a text shows the celestial government icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla puts it in front of the word, for example in the names of the celestial ruler and vassal opinion modifiers.

label: Celestial government
summary: The game concept Celestial Government: a bureaucratic form of government where the liege appoints characters as civilian or military governors.
details: `[celestials|E]` in a text shows the word "Celestials" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Ceremonial claimant faction
summary: The game concept Ceremonial Claimant Faction: a faction that wants to put its claimant in place as the ceremonial monarch.
details: `[ceremonial_claimant_faction|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. If the faction wins, the sitting ceremonial monarch must hand their title to the claimant, and every faction member gets a hook on the claimant. Vanilla uses it in the interaction that founds such a faction.

label: Ceremonial claimant faction
summary: The game concept Ceremonial Claimant Faction: a faction that wants to put its claimant in place as the ceremonial monarch.
details: `[ceremonial_claimant_factions|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. If such a faction wins, the ceremonial monarch hands their title to the claimant, and the members get a hook on the claimant. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Ceremonial house
summary: The game concept Ceremonial House: the house of a realm's ceremonial monarch.
details: `[ceremonial_house|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The ceremonial monarch's concept text adds that it is the most esteemed bloodline in the realm even though it does not rule directly. Vanilla uses it in Japanese government and administration texts.

label: Ceremonial monarch
summary: The game concept Ceremonial Monarch: a ruler who reigns in name only while a ruling regent holds the real power, as in Japan.
details: `[ceremonial_liege|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. In practice the ceremonial monarch is a figurehead and a vassal, and every member of their house belongs to the ceremonial house. Vanilla uses it in court position, interaction and AI texts.

label: Ceremonial monarch's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Ceremonial Monarch, a ruler who reigns in name only while a ruling regent holds the real power.
details: `[ceremonial_liege_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in Japanese texts about the ceremonial monarch's heir and line of succession.

label: Ruling regency
summary: The game concept Ruling Regent, here as the word "Ruling Regency": the rule of a top liege who governs in practice on behalf of a ceremonial monarch.
details: `[ceremonial_regency|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. In Japan the regent's position may be called kampaku or shogun, depending on the political situation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Ruling regent
summary: The game concept Ruling Regent: any top liege who rules in practice on behalf of a ceremonial monarch, such as the Japanese Ten'no.
details: `[ceremonial_regent|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The position's name can change with the political situation; in Japan it may be kampaku or shogun. Vanilla uses it in the texts of the faction that tries to oust the regent.

label: Ruling regent
summary: The game concept Ruling Regent: any top liege who rules in practice on behalf of a ceremonial monarch.
details: `[ceremonial_regents|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it when counting a dynasty's previous regents in the Japanese government texts.

label: Challenger head of faith
summary: The game concept Challenger Head of Faith: a rival head of faith raised against the head of faith of the mainline rite.
details: `[challenger_hof|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A ruler can sponsor a member of their clergy as challenger, and a clergy ruler or a ruler of a faith with a temporal head of faith can declare themselves instead. A sponsored challenger takes the sponsor's rite and becomes their external clerical puppet. Vanilla uses it in antipope hook, title and petition texts.

label: Chance of infection
summary: The game concept Chance of Infection: how likely a character is to catch a disease from an ongoing epidemic.
details: `[chance_of_infection|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Chancellor
summary: The game concept Chancellor: the councillor who handles diplomacy, both inside and outside the realm.
details: `[chancellor|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in council texts, for example the warning that you have no chancellor.

label: Chancellor
summary: The game concept Chancellor: the councillor who handles diplomacy, both inside and outside the realm.
details: `[chancellors|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in faith texts about who may be appointed to the council.

label: Character
summary: The game concept Character: a person in the game, noble or lowborn, landed or unlanded, with their own skills, traits and goals.
details: `[character|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Characters appear as rulers, courtiers and guests, and can be interacted with while within diplomatic range. Vanilla uses it widely, for example in achievement texts.

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death: a character dying, which starts succession for rulers.
details: `[character_death|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. When the player's character dies, play continues as their player heir, or the game ends if there is no valid heir. Vanilla uses it in the funeral text.

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death, shown as the word "Death".
details: `[character_death_death|E]` in a text shows the noun "Death" linked to the concept's explanation, which says death starts succession and the player continues as their heir. Vanilla uses it in the texts about the warning before a natural death.

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death, shown as the plural word "deaths".
details: `[character_death_deaths|E]` in a text shows the plural noun linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in East Asian texts listing which kinds of death are possible, such as natural or religious deaths.

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death, shown as the verb "die".
details: `[character_death_die|E]` in a text shows the verb linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in sentences such as "you die" in trait and diarchy texts.

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death, shown as the verb "dies".
details: `[character_death_dies|E]` in a text shows the verb linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in sentences such as "when the current ruler dies".

label: Character death
summary: The game concept Character Death, shown as the word "Dying".
details: `[character_death_dying|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Character interaction
summary: The game concept Interaction, shown as "Character Interaction": an action one character takes towards another.
details: `[character_interaction|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Some interactions need the target's approval and some do not; most are opened by right-clicking a character. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that name a specific interaction.

label: Character modifier
summary: The game concept Character Modifier: a modifier held by a character that changes things like their personality, skills or income.
details: `[character_modifier|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Unlike traits, character modifiers are usually temporary. Vanilla uses it in a decision tooltip that grants a temporary one.

label: Character modifier
summary: The game concept Character Modifier: a modifier held by a character that changes things like their personality, skills or income.
details: `[character_modifiers|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Unlike traits, they are usually temporary. Vanilla uses it in relation and single combat texts.

label: Personality
summary: The game concept Personality, shown as "Character Personality": how a character behaves towards others, mainly set by their personality traits.
details: `[character_personality|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A ruler's behavior can also be changed by some modifiers and special traits. Vanilla uses it in the AI personality summary tooltip.

label: Character's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Character, a person in the game.
details: `[character_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example about a character's partition share.

label: Character
summary: The game concept Character: a person in the game, noble or lowborn, landed or unlanded, with their own skills, traits and goals.
details: `[characters|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it widely, for example in court type and achievement texts.

label: Characters'
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Character, a person in the game.
details: `[characters_possessive|E]` in a text shows the word "Characters'" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Child
summary: The game concept Child: a character younger than 16.
details: `[child|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in achievement and court position texts.

label: Child health
summary: The game concept Child Health: health penalties that only hit children, for example from measles.
details: `[child_health|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A penalty to child health adds on top of the normal health penalties, even when both come from the same trait. Vanilla uses it as the name of the child health modifier.

label: Child's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Child, a character younger than 16.
details: `[child_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in interaction and court event texts, such as a child's house or education.

label: Childhood trait
summary: The game concept Childhood Trait: a trait every child gains while growing up, such as Rowdy or Charming.
details: `[childhood_trait|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The trait hints at which education focus suits the child best, and vanilla's education texts say a good match improves the education trait they get.

label: Child
summary: The game concept Child: a character younger than 16.
details: `[children|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it widely, for example in trait and court position texts.

label: Children's examination
summary: The game concept Children's Examination: the first level of the imperial examinations, open to children from a minimum age set by a script value.
details: `[childrens_examination|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Parents send their children to it with an interaction. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Children's examination (icon)
summary: The icon of the game concept Children's Examination, the first level of the imperial examinations.
details: `[childrens_examination_i|E]` in a text shows the child examination icon linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Christendom
summary: The game concept Christendom: the realms of all independent Christian rulers who belong to the Christian Church situation.
details: `[christendom|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in great project and concept texts.

label: Christian
summary: The game concept Christian: someone who follows the Christian religion.
details: `[christian|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in government and important action texts.

label: Christian's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Christian, someone who follows the Christian religion.
details: `[christian_possessive|E]` in a text shows the word "Christian's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Christian
summary: The game concept Christian: someone who follows the Christian religion.
details: `[christians|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the Christian Church situation's events.

label: Church authority
summary: The game concept Church Authority: how much power a theocratic ruler holds over their clergy and vassals.
details: `[church_authority|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. It has four levels; raising it costs piety and prestige, depending on the level and the ruler's learning skill, and vassals dislike higher levels. Vanilla uses it in decision and law texts.

label: Church centralization
summary: The game concept Church Centralization: how centralized the Church's authority and finances are.
details: `[church_centralization|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The stronger it is, the more income flows up the clerical hierarchy; the types are minimal, mild and strong centralization. Vanilla uses it in the church obligations concept text.

label: Church holding
summary: The game concept Church Holdings, shown as "Church Holding": a temple controlled by a realm priest.
details: `[church_holding|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. In faiths with the lay clergy doctrine there are no church holdings, and secular rulers can hold temples without penalty. Vanilla uses it in holding type and church income texts.

label: Church holding
summary: The game concept Church Holdings: temples controlled by a realm priest.
details: `[church_holdings|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. In faiths with the lay clergy doctrine there are none, and secular rulers can hold temples without penalty. Vanilla uses it in the income and levy lines of the theocratic lease.

label: Church obligations
summary: The game concept Church Obligations: all the dues taken from church holding income together.
details: `[church_obligations|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The dues go to the religious superior, the head of faith and/or the local secular ruler; church centralization and secular obligations are examples. Vanilla uses it in the expense and income split lines of the theocratic lease.

label: Church holding
summary: The game concept Church Holdings: temples controlled by a realm priest.
details: `[church_property|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation; this key is the concept itself. In faiths with the lay clergy doctrine there are no church holdings. Vanilla uses it in the effects where a theocracy starts or stops endorsing a ruler.

label: Rodrigo's loyalty
summary: The game concept Rodrigo's Loyalty: whether El Cid stays loyal to his liege during his exile.
details: `[cid_loyalty|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Staying loyal may win back the liege's favor and his old position; turning disloyal may open special options to become an independent ruler. Vanilla uses it in El Cid's story texts that show loyalty to the liege.

label: Province
summary: The game concept Province, shown as "Circuit": a title held by a governor inside a bureaucratic realm.
details: `[circuit|E]` in a text shows the word "Circuit" linked to the concept's explanation. Each province has a province administration that strongly affects what it gives. Vanilla uses it as the Chinese government's name for the province concept.

label: Province administration
summary: The game concept Province Administration, shown as "Circuit Administration": the specialization set for a province of a bureaucratic realm.
details: `[circuit_administration|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. The liege and the governor can set it, and only one can be active per province. Vanilla uses it as the Chinese government's name for this concept.

label: Province
summary: The game concept Province, shown as "Circuits": titles held by governors inside a bureaucratic realm.
details: `[circuits|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the plural of the Chinese government's name for provinces.

label: City holding
summary: The game concept City Holding, shown as "Cities": the richest holding type, which gives more taxes than levies.
details: `[cities|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Cities belong with republics, and holding one under any playable government form always brings a penalty. Vanilla uses it in holding type and building slot texts.

label: City holding
summary: The game concept City Holding, shown as "City": the richest holding type, which gives more taxes than levies.
details: `[city|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Holding a city under any playable government form always brings a penalty. Vanilla uses it in decision and concept texts.

label: City holding
summary: The game concept City Holding: the richest holding type, which gives more taxes than levies.
details: `[city_holding|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. City holdings belong with republics, and holding one under any playable government form always brings a penalty. Vanilla uses it in cultural tradition and holding type texts.

label: City holding
summary: The game concept City Holding: the richest holding type, which gives more taxes than levies.
details: `[city_holdings|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in holding lease and cultural tradition texts.

label: Civil war
summary: The game concept Civil War: a war in which vassals and/or counties revolt against their liege.
details: `[civil_war|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Most come from a faction whose demands were refused, and losing one often costs more than the faction first asked for. Vanilla uses it in faction and concept texts.

label: Civil war
summary: The game concept Civil War: a war in which vassals and/or counties revolt against their liege.
details: `[civil_wars|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a concept text noting that civil wars are excluded from the offensive war penalty.

label: Civilian career path
summary: The game concept Civilian Career Path: the path of rulers who focus on administration rather than war.
details: `[civilian_career|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Such rulers are appointed to civilian circuits, and their merit grows with buildings built and taxes paid to their liege. Vanilla uses it in the Chinese decision texts about having or changing to this career.
